data.body:
Two more cases, from 2a3d-9d00's re-review at d74d53a5ffd. Both dropped under veto:cited-reference-inaccurate, both verified correct against the tree. That makes 5 of 5 checked drops wrong, across three tickets (c159 x2, 2a3d x2, 28d0 x1).

Case 4 — finding: plan cites 'AGENTS.md:215,428' as the lines already referencing the packaged guides. Measured on origin/main d74d53a5ffd: writing-a-passing-plan.md is cited at AGENTS.md:225 and passing-code-review.md at :443. The finding's own correction (:225, :443) was exact. Dropped anyway.

Case 5 — finding: plan cites 'registry.py:665-666' as naming the packaged basenames. Measured: the AUTHOR_GUIDES entries are at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:615-616. The plan also gave a bare filename where the repo has two candidate paths, which the finding noted. Dropped anyway.

Both strengthen the hypothesis in the description: the veto appears to compare the finding's cited location against the plan's cited location and read the mismatch as the FINDING being inaccurate, when the mismatch is exactly what a correct finding about a wrong citation looks like. It fires precisely when the plan is wrong, which is when the finding is most needed.

Sample now: 5 drops checked, 5 correct, 0 incorrect. No case has yet been found where the veto suppressed a genuinely inaccurate finding.
